name: La Silla Observatory
place: La Silla, Coquimbo Region (Atacama Desert edge)
description: ESO's first observatory in Chile, at 2,400 m under some of the darkest skies on Earth. Its main telescopes are the ESO 3.6 m, the New Technology Telescope and the MPG/ESO 2.2 m.
highlights: Its HARPS spectrograph is described as the most successful finder of low-mass exoplanets.
HARPS was one of the instruments that found Proxima b in 2016, the nearest known exoplanet.
La Silla followed SN 1987A, the nearest supernova seen in modern times, from 1987.
